mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in FEDFUNDS above 5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary regime, which increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the effect reverses during a recession.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 exceeding 2% signals a significant weakening in aggregate demand, which depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the GDP decline is not followed by equity market underperformance.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in UNRATE above 4.5% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which pressures firms to raise wages and prices, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or inflation does not rise concurrently.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals weakening industrial production, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month MA for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the decline in industrial production is not accompanied by earnings downgrades.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline in both GDPC1 and HOUST signals a broad-based contraction in economic activity and housing demand, which reduces corporate revenues and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of co-declining episodes, or the effect is absent during a housing-specific shock.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in FEDFUNDS of more than 0.75 percentage points in a single month, combined with a concurrent rise in CPIAUCSL above 3% month-over-month, signals aggressive tightening and accelerating inflation, which erodes real equity valuations and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS jumps > 0.75% in one month AND CPIAUCSL > 3% MoM
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or CPI does not sustain the increase.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in PAYEMS above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which supports consumer spending and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month MA for five consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the labor market expansion is not accompanied by wage growth.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in RSAFS exceeding 5% signals a surge in consumer savings, which typically precedes a reduction in consumption and weaker corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the savings increase is not followed by a decline in consumption.
